author: Aryn Yklas
unitBoundaryScope: Generic errno classification, fixed capability/error transport, tracefs permission-versus-absence classification, missing metadata and target refusal only. Unit inputs do not install or qualify seccomp, effective host capability, LSM, tracefs ACL or PID isolation; the real-kernel cases below do.
denyingLayer: unknown unless independently established by retained operator-controlled policy evidence (an operator-supplied unit property, an audit line naming the profile, an observed mount or /proc option, a capability set read back from /proc, a flip of the verdict when only that layer is removed); EPERM/EACCES alone do not identify a layer
helperCommand: go run ./fixtures/nativeperf/helper-smoke/drive --unit soundpost-perf-acquire.service --scenarios capture,offcpu (the real cmd/soundpost-perf-acquire under the shipped unit, plus an operator drop-in per layer)
kernels: qualification: 6.1.0-54 (Debian, lsm list lockdown,capability,landlock,yama,apparmor,tomoyo,bpf) on d12 and cg1; 6.6.162 (mainline, lsm list lockdown,capability,landlock,yama,apparmor) on k66. perf_event_paranoid was 1 on all three before and after every run and was only read. sp-oci (6.12.74, Docker 26.1.5, paranoid 3 Debian patch) is case evidence only.
evidence: Wave 33 (lane 4, L4w33Perm): .superpowers/sdd/approved-product/l4w33-evidence/L4w33Perm/{perm-matrix-sp-cg1-final.txt,perm-matrix-sp-q-d12-run1.txt,perm-matrix-sp-q-d12-tracefs-final.txt,perm-matrix-sp-q-k66-final.txt,perm-matrix-lsm-*-final.txt,helper-rows-sp-q-d12-final.txt,helper-rows-sp-q-k66-final.txt,bpf-lsm-sp-q-d12-run1.txt,bpf-lsm-sp-cg1-final.txt,tracefs-mountopt-*.txt,final-checks-*.txt}; scripts perm-matrix.sh, helper-rows.sh, bpf-lsm.sh. Wave 31 (NativeA): l4w31-evidence/NativeA/{permission-cases-sp-q-d12.txt,permission-cases-sp-q-k66.txt,oci-seccomp-probe.txt,oci-capability-probe-variants.txt,oci-container-smoke-*.txt}.

cases.name: seccomp-denied
cases.change: Operator-owned filter denies perf_event_open with EPERM (transient systemd unit property, and a drop-in of the installed helper unit); CAP_PERFMON, paranoid, tracefs and target visibility untouched
cases.expected: CPU denied; no samples; no unconfined fallback; a filter that does not name perf_event_open must not deny
cases.observed: d12, k66, cg1, probe in a transient unit as root with every capability: SystemCallFilter=~perf_event_open (EPERM): cpu, off_cpu, runqueue_split denied, reason permission_denied, no samples, while /proc/self/status shows Seccomp: 2 and CapEff 000001ffffffffff. Controls: no filter (Seccomp: 0) supported; a filter denying only sethostname (Seccomp: 2) supported; the same perf_event_open filter with action ENOSYS is reported unsupported/event_unavailable, not denied (the probe classifies by errno). Real helper (shipped unit, drop-in SystemCallFilter=~perf_event_open) on d12 and k66: authorized and capture both refused 'native profiling: denied: permission_denied', fd_before == fd_after, no samples; control drop-in denying only sethostname: capture opens with 592 and 583 samples; shipped unit before and after the layered rows: 593/587 (d12) and 591/583 (k66) samples. sp-oci (6.12): the audited profile with only perf_event_open set to EPERM: sandboxprobe reports EPERM; the shipped profile itself lets the real helper capture 591 samples.
cases.denyingLayerEvidence: the layer is named because the filter was operator-supplied (unit property / drop-in) and the verdict flips when only that filter changes (S1/S2 and H2 are the controls)

cases.name: host-capability-denied
cases.change: Operator-owned account or namespace lacks the effective host CAP_PERFMON; host perf_event_paranoid unchanged
cases.expected: Real upstream perf scope decision reported; no assumption that a namespace capability grants host scope; capability layer separable from the tracefs layer
cases.observed: d12, k66, cg1 (paranoid 1), 2x2 with the tracefs layer held constant, same account (uid 65534), same-uid target: PERFMON absent + tracefs granted: cpu supported (upstream paranoid decision for an own task), off_cpu denied permission_denied with the account able to read events/sched/sched_switch/id, CapEff 0000000000000000 (the capability layer alone); PERFMON present + tracefs granted: everything supported (control); PERFMON present + host root-only tracefs: off_cpu denied with the id unreadable (the tracefs layer alone, see tracefs-dac-denied); both absent: denied. User-namespace root with every capability only inside the userns, own-process target: cpu supported, scheduler tracepoints denied permission_denied although the userns root reads the tracefs id; the same host root without the user namespace: everything supported. Real helper (d12, k66): unit with the same tracefs grant and CAP_PERFMON removed (bounding set without it, no ambient): capture opens (555 and 586 samples), the CPU+scheduler request is refused permission_denied; with PERFMON kept the same request opens with samples (590 and 464). sp-oci (paranoid 3, Debian patch): no capabilities, PERFMON, and PERFMON+SYS_PTRACE+DAC_READ_SEARCH all give cpu denied; a privileged container is supported; the real helper in a PERFMON-only container is refused permission_denied. The extra capability the Debian kernel needs was not isolated.
cases.denyingLayerEvidence: CapEff read back from /proc inside the probed process, the id file readable by the same account, and the flip of the verdict when only CAP_PERFMON is added

cases.name: lsm-denied
cases.change: Operator-supplied disposable LSM policy refuses the helper's access to the target while capability and seccomp allow it: uniquely named AppArmor profiles l4w33-perm-* loaded with apparmor_parser and unloaded afterwards, and (6.1 only) a BPF-LSM policy on the security_perf_event_open hook
cases.expected: Generic permission denial; retain the kernel audit line that names the profile instead of inferring the cause from EPERM
cases.observed: cg1, d12 (6.1.0-54) and k66 (6.6.162): probe confined by profile l4w33-perm-test (capability, network, signal, unix and all file access allowed, no ptrace rule): 'target identity unavailable: denied/permission_denied'; the kernel log carries apparmor="DENIED" operation="ptrace" profile="l4w33-perm-test" requested_mask="read" denied_mask="read" peer="unconfined" (comm capability, readlink, cat). The same rules in complain mode pass and log apparmor="ALLOWED"; the same confinement with 'ptrace,' passes with no denial; unconfined passes. Raw perf_event_open(2) by an uid-65534 account without capabilities on a same-uid target: opens unconfined and under the allowing profile, EACCES under the denying profile with the DENIED ptrace audit line (AppArmor mediates perf_event_open through ptrace_may_access); a perfmon_capable caller skips that check inside the kernel, so root with every capability opens under the denying profile and loses only the /proc identity step. Real helper (shipped unit + AppArmorProfile= drop-in) on d12 and k66: profile without ptrace rule: authorized and capture refused permission_denied, audit lines apparmor="DENIED" operation="ptrace" profile="l4w33-perm-unit-deny" comm="soundpost-perf-"; identical profile with 'ptrace,': 593 and 583 samples. 6.1 (cg1, d12): BPF_PROG_TYPE_LSM program on bpf_lsm_perf_event_open scoped to test uid 65533 with CAP_PERFMON only: cpu denied permission_denied while attached (link_type tracing, attach_type 27), supported before attach and after the link is closed; root unaffected; an allow program attached the same way changes nothing. k66's lsm list has no bpf: no perf_event_open hook there, the AppArmor ptrace mediation is the qualification-kernel LSM evidence on 6.6. All profiles unloaded and verified absent (profile count 0); the BPF link dies with its process. sp-oci (6.12): docker-default AppArmor denies the helper (permission_denied) while unconfined captures, audit line apparmor="DENIED" operation="ptrace" profile="docker-default".
cases.denyingLayerEvidence: kernel audit line naming the operator-supplied profile; complain-mode and ptrace-allowed controls with identical confinement; BPF link fdinfo and attach/detach flip

cases.name: tracefs-denied
cases.change: Operator-owned disposable mount namespace hides tracefs (empty tmpfs over /sys/kernel/tracing and /sys/kernel/debug) while self CPU perf remains permitted
cases.expected: CPU supported and off-CPU unavailable independently; not successful full qualification
cases.observed: d12, k66, cg1: root caller: cpu supported, off_cpu and runqueue_split unsupported reason tracefs_unavailable, scheduler_event_open unsupported (0 files visible in the mount). Helper-shaped account (uid 65534, only CAP_PERFMON): identical (the account reads ENOENT for events/sched/sched_switch/id). Hiding only /sys/kernel/tracing while /sys/kernel/debug (root-only 0700) still holds the fallback path is a mixed ENOENT + EACCES lookup and is reported as the permission denial (off_cpu denied): an observed permission refusal takes precedence over absence because the operator must resolve it.
cases.denyingLayerEvidence: observed mount namespace content (0 files) and ENOENT read by the account

cases.name: tracefs-dac-denied
cases.change: Helper-shaped account (uid 65534, only CAP_PERFMON, same-uid target) against the host tracefs as mounted (root:root 0700 directories 0750 inodes 0440); no grant
cases.expected: CPU supported; off-CPU explicitly DENIED (permission_denied), distinct from an absent tracefs
cases.observed: d12, k66, cg1: cpu supported, off_cpu/runqueue_split/scheduler_event_open denied reason permission_denied; the account itself reads 'Permission denied' for events/sched/sched_switch/id and tracing_on. Defect found and fixed in this wave: the probe used to report this as unsupported/tracefs_unavailable (tracepointID discarded the errno), while the real helper path already reported permission_denied; Probe now reports a refused tracefs as denied/permission_denied and an absent one as unsupported/tracefs_unavailable (TestPerfPermissionDimensions/tracefs-dac-denial-is-denied-and-absence-is-unsupported, red on cg1 before the change, mutants killed). Real helper (shipped unit, CAP_PERFMON only) on d12 and k66: capture opens with 591/584 samples while the CPU+scheduler request is refused 'native profiling: denied: permission_denied' in the same helper run: CPU-only capture coexists with an explicit denied off-CPU capability.
cases.denyingLayerEvidence: observed 0700 root-only tracefs, EACCES read by the same account, and the verdict flip in tracefs-grant-allowed

cases.name: tracefs-grant-allowed
cases.change: Positive control for tracefs-dac-denied: the same account, target and capabilities with an operator-owned grant that changes no host state: a read-only view of the host tracefs events/ subtree in a private mount namespace (0755 tmpfs at /sys/kernel/tracing, bind of events, read-only) plus the group that owns the 0750/0440 inodes
cases.expected: off-CPU goes from denied to supported for a CAP_PERFMON-only non-root account without any host tracefs change
cases.observed: d12, k66, cg1: with the view: the account reads the tracepoint id (319 on 6.1, 330 on 6.6), cpu and off_cpu and runqueue_split supported, scheduler_event_open supported; the host tracefs root stayed root:root 0700 with the same number of tracefs mounts, paranoid unchanged. Real helper under systemd (d12, k66): drop-in TemporaryFileSystem=/sys/kernel/tracing:ro,mode=0755 + BindReadOnlyPaths=/sys/kernel/tracing/events + SupplementaryGroups=root (and ProtectKernelTunables=no: the shipped read-only /sys remount is re-applied over such a view): capture 590/581 and CPU+scheduler request 'opened' with 590/464 samples, against the same unit without the view refused permission_denied. Mount options are NOT host-neutral: tracefs is a single global superblock, so mounting it in a private mount namespace with mode=0755,uid=,gid= changed the host's tracefs root to 755 65534:65534 (cg1, restored to 700 0:0 and verified); a remount with gid=65534,mode=0750 reaches the existing children (events and id become group 65534) and let the account read the id and open off-CPU (cg1, host-wide for one probe, restored and verified identical). No POSIX ACL exists on tracefs and setfacl is not installed.
cases.denyingLayerEvidence: n/a (grant); the observed events view, the readable id file and the unchanged host root

cases.name: target-visibility-denied
cases.change: Operator-owned disposable PID/mount namespace hides the authorized target's proc identity
cases.expected: Target refusal before acquisition; no hostPID escalation
cases.observed: d12, k66, cg1: a new PID namespace with its own /proc and a host target PID: 'target identity unavailable: not_visible_or_invalid' (no acquisition attempted); control: a target created inside the same namespace resolves and cpu is supported (off_cpu unsupported there: raw scheduler PIDs are init-namespace PIDs).
cases.denyingLayerEvidence: the namespace was operator-created; the control target in the same namespace passes

cases.name: target-dac-ptrace-denied
cases.change: Foreign-uid (root-owned) target, /proc hidepid=0, account uid 65534 with only CAP_PERFMON (new PID namespace + private /proc)
cases.expected: Target refusal as a permission denial, separable from invisibility
cases.observed: d12, k66, cg1: the account lists 7 pids and reads /proc/T/stat (ok) but readlink /proc/T/ns/pid is refused (ptrace_may_access, DAC); the probe prints 'target identity unavailable: denied/permission_denied'. CAP_SYS_PTRACE added: the link resolves and cpu is supported (control). CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH added instead: unchanged, still denied (negative control: it does not grant ptrace access). Same-uid target: resolves with PERFMON only.
cases.denyingLayerEvidence: stat and stat-file read succeed while only the ptrace-gated ns/pid link fails; the flip with CAP_SYS_PTRACE

cases.name: hidepid-denied
cases.change: Operator-owned disposable PID namespace remounts /proc with hidepid=1 (noaccess), 2 (invisible) or 4 (ptraceable); the account targets a process of another uid
cases.expected: Target refusal before acquisition; each mount option's own effect observable
cases.observed: d12, k66, cg1, foreign-uid target, PERFMON only: hidepid=1: the dir is listed, read of /proc/T/stat 'Operation not permitted', probe 'denied/permission_denied'; hidepid=2 and 4: the entry is gone (stat 'No such file', 5 pids listed instead of 7), probe 'not_visible_or_invalid'. With CAP_SYS_PTRACE every mode lists 7 pids and resolves the target and cpu is supported (control for each mode). Same-uid target resolves under hidepid=0, 2 and 4 with PERFMON only. CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH adds nothing except one kernel quirk recorded as observed: at hidepid=4 with it, stat says ENOENT, the stat-file read says EPERM and the probe reports denied/permission_denied instead of not_visible.
cases.denyingLayerEvidence: the remount option was operator-applied inside the namespace; the listing count and the errno of /proc/T/stat independently show which option applies

deploymentPrerequisites.systemd: Use packaging/systemd/soundpost-perf-acquire.service only after dedicated UID, root-owned policy, proc/tracefs/cgroup access and PERFMON approval. Scheduler off-CPU additionally needs an operator grant of tracefs (group access plus a traversable events/ view, or a host tracefs gid=/mode= option, which is host-wide); the shipped ProtectKernelTunables=yes re-applies a read-only /sys over a unit-private TemporaryFileSystem view, so a view-based grant needs ProtectKernelTunables=no.
deploymentPrerequisites.container: cap_drop ALL; cap_add PERFMON only after operator approval; audited deploy/seccomp/soundpost-perf.json; read-only approved proc/tracefs/cgroup views; read-only host /etc/machine-id; private Unix socket mount; no network exposure
deploymentPrerequisites.compose: Separate optional helper service with same container restrictions; exporter shares dedicated local UID and private runtime socket only, never tenant ingress identity
deploymentPrerequisites.kubernetes: Optional helper with drop ALL/add PERFMON, allowPrivilegeEscalation false, Localhost audited seccomp, read-only approved metadata mounts including /etc/machine-id; target PID visibility and every host mount require explicit authorization; Pod Security rejection remains denied
